title: Scale-aware quant kernel mediator and prefill/decoding scheduler
creator: Rahul Singh
description: Problem: Our mixed-precision paths (INT8 and experimental FP8) incur non-trivial conversion overheads at kernel boundaries (scale/zero-point handling and ephemeral float<->quant conversions). That overhead erodes the benefits of quantized kernels for short sequences and during prefill-heavy workloads. Goal: Implement a scale-aware kernel mediator and a prefill/decoding scheduler that minimizes conversion work, picks kernel variants based on per-request sequence distribution, and fuses or amortizes conversion steps where possible. Outcomes should include measurable end-to-end token/sec improvements for short to medium sequence workloads and no regression on long-sequence throughput or numeric correctness beyond accepted tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel mediator selects INT8/FP8/mixed-precision path with <2% PPL regression on standard eval prompts when quant path chosen
End-to-end decode latency reduced by >=12% for 8-64 token responses on representative chat workloads in our bench cluster (p50), compared to current INT8 path
Per-token CPU/GPU cycles due to format conversion reduced by >=30% when mediator chooses fused conversion/fallbacks
Integration with kernel registry: mediator consults kernel fingerprints and selects compatible fused-attention kernels at runtime
Automated tests covering path selection heuristics, fallback correctness, and numerical tolerances added
Documentation updated (architecture doc + runbook) and rollout plan with canary thresholds defined
experiments: Microbench: fused INT8-attn kernel reduced conversion time by 42% vs separate dequant stage on 80-token prefill (A100, batch=4)
FP8 path experiments show 8-12% throughput gains on long sequences but higher variance at short sequences due to per-token FP<->INT conversions
Heuristic: favor INT8 fused kernels for decode if avg response length < 64 and KV cache hit ratio > 0.6 — yielded 15% median latency improvement in synthetic chat traces
tasks: API: Add mediator abstraction layer that exposes choose_kernel(request_meta, workload_stats) -> kernel_tag
Runtime: Extend kernel registry schema with 'conversion_cost' and 'fused_conversion' flags
Kernels: Add small fused conversion+attn kernels for popular model dims (e.g., 4096/16 heads) and quant layouts
Scheduler: Implement prefill/decoder scheduling policy that batches conversions across concurrent prefill requests when safe
Bench: Create bench scenarios (chat-short, summary-medium, long-compute) and baseline against runtime-1.19
Tests: Add unit/integration tests for mediator decisions and numerical tolerance checks
Docs: Author runbook for canary rollout with perf/regression alerts

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive fusion reduces conversion overhead but increases kernel count — mitigate via codegen + autotuning to keep footprint manageable.
Fallback policy: if fused kernel not available or numerical tolerance fails autotest, fall back to mixed-precision path with explicit amortized conversion.
Rollout: start with hosted API pool (non-enterprise) and a 5% canary, ramp on bench metrics and no new errors in logs
